analysis.title: Belden Inc. (BDC): Good bookings especially in the datacenter market, although Ruckus supply chain tightness limiting near-term results; 3Q26 wrap
key_insights: Belden reported 3Q26 revenue of $966 mn (+38% y/y, +11% organically), above GS at $960 mn, the Street (FactSet) at $962 mn and the $950-$970 mn guidance range. Non-GAAP EPS of $2.26 was in line with the Street at $2.26 and $0.01 below GS at $2.27.
Orders were a record $1,017 mn (+46% y/y, +16% organically) with a book-to-bill ratio of 1.05X. Orders rose about 30% in both the Smart Buildings and Automation end markets.

Belden signed an agreement to supply $100 mn of fiber assemblies in 2027. Management now expects the datacenter business to grow more than 50% next year to about $275 mn of revenue. The datacenter business includes both AI and traditional enterprise datacenter customers.

Ruckus orders were up 10% with a book-to-bill of 1.09X, but Ruckus revenue fell 6% y/y in 3Q on shipment delays tied to component availability and supplier lead times, about $10-$15 mn of lost revenue in the quarter. Management expects a measured supply recovery into 2027 and says demand and backlogs remain healthy.
4Q26 guidance: revenue $960-$980 mn (midpoint $970 mn vs GS prior $948 mn and Street $962 mn) and non-GAAP EPS $2.20-$2.35 (midpoint $2.28 vs GS prior $2.18 and Street $2.27).

Adjusted EBITDA was $171 mn (17.7% of revenue) vs GS $171 mn (17.9%) and Street $171 mn (17.8%). Non-GAAP gross margin was 41.5% vs GS 41.6%. Adjusted free cash flow was about $81.9 mn. No shares were repurchased and about $2 mn went to dividends.

Belden closed the Ruckus Networks acquisition from Vistance Networks for about $1.85 bn on July 1. It is expected to be immediately accretive to adjusted EPS and to expand gross and adjusted EBITDA margins in the first full year. Belden expects net leverage below 3.0X within the first full year and targets 1.5X by 2029.

GS keeps its Buy rating. It cites datacenter wins for 2027 growth, factory automation tailwinds (over 30% order growth in Smart Buildings and Automation) and a broader industrial cyclical recovery. It is also encouraged by margin growth from Ruckus, which has above-corporate-average EBITDA margins, and from underlying growth despite input cost pressure.

GS cut its 12-month price target to $151 from $161, based on 14X (from 15X, on lower peer multiples) applied to normalized EPS of $10.75 (unchanged). EPS estimates for 2026/27/28 moved to $8.65/$10.05/$11.25 from $8.55/$10.25/$11.15, reflecting higher revenue and higher interest expense.

market_movers.rationale: GS cut its price target to $151 from $161 on a lower multiple (14X vs 15X) applied to unchanged normalized EPS of $10.75. It keeps the Buy on datacenter, factory automation and industrial recovery drivers, with 40.5% upside from $107.48.

earnings_insights: BDC 3Q26 reported 10/29/2026: revenue $966 mn vs GS $960 mn, Street (FactSet) $962 mn, guidance midpoint $960 mn. Non-GAAP EPS $2.26 reported vs GS est $2.27, Street est $2.26, guidance midpoint $2.23.

BDC 4Q26 guidance: revenue $960-$980 mn (midpoint $970 mn) vs GS prior est $948.2 mn and Street est (FactSet) $962.0 mn. Non-GAAP EPS $2.20-$2.35 (midpoint $2.28) vs GS prior est $2.18 and Street est $2.27.

GS estimates, FY26E/27E/28E EPS (diluted, pre-exceptionals) $8.65/$10.05/$11.25 vs prior $8.55/$10.25/$11.15. FY26E/27E/28E revenue $3,383.2 mn/$3,974.3 mn/$4,165.5 mn vs prior $3,354.9 mn/$3,941.0 mn/$4,121.5 mn. FY25 actual EPS was $7.54 and revenue $2,715.2 mn.
3Q26 orders were $1,017 mn, +21.7% q/q and +45.7% y/y. Non-GAAP operating income was $152.0 mn (15.7% margin) vs GS $152.5 mn (15.9%).
risk_factors: Revenue outlook, including industrial (orders and revenue have historically tracked industrial indicators such as the ISM index, and some industrial data points have been weak) and Enterprise (sluggish commercial office/smart building and telecom capex).
Margins: GS expects mix shift to full solutions sales to lift margins, but pricing pressure and execution risk could hurt.
Belden's ability to keep growing through M&A and inorganic investment in higher-growth areas such as fiber connectivity.
The extent to which government stimulus programs drive incremental demand, which depends on how funding is allocated.
Ruckus supply constraints from component availability and supplier lead times (about $10-$15 mn of lost 3Q revenue).

tension_points.bull_case: Record orders of $1,017 mn, a $100 mn fiber supply deal, datacenter revenue expected to grow more than 50% to about $275 mn in 2027, and over 30% order growth in Smart Buildings and Automation support growth, with Ruckus backlogs healthy.
tension_points.bear_case: Ruckus revenue fell 6% y/y on component shortages and supplier lead times, costing about $10-$15 mn of revenue in 3Q, and management expects only a measured supply recovery into 2027. GS also flags weak industrial data points and sluggish commercial office and telecom capex.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A weak ISM index and industrial data, which GS says historically track Belden's revenue and orders, or Ruckus supply recovery slower than the measured pace management expects into 2027.
